source_credit: Naval Ravikant: tweetstorms and The Almanack of Naval Ravikant (Eric Jorgenson, 2020). Plain one-line maxims in our own words.

entries.text: Build things that keep earning when you are away. Chasing status or quick cash wastes time.
Hourly pay alone will not make you rich. Own a piece of the business you build.
Get paid for what you know and decide, not just for the hours you put in.
Find something people want but cannot easily get yet. Then offer it to many of them.
Your hours run out. Set up software and videos that keep working when you are away.
Make a video, post or simple tool once. It can bring in customers for years.
Learn what truly interests you. Skills anyone can be taught make you easy to replace.
The best skills are learned by doing the work, not from a class. Keep doing it.
Work with people you can stick with for years. Small gains add up over time.
Picture the payoff of waiting clearly. Then waiting takes much less willpower.
Pick partners who are smart, driven and honest. If honesty is missing, walk away.
Never cheat to win. Even if it works, you become someone who cheats.
Put your own name on your work and own the results. People trust and reward that.
Stay honest year after year. A good name lets you take bigger chances later.
Make calls you can stand behind and own the outcome. Good judgment is your best tool.
Most problems come from seeing things wrong. Take time to check how things really work.
If you cannot write it down simply, you do not understand it yet. Write it out.
Skip petty fights. What you build matters more than who you beat in an argument.
Calm and good mood can be practiced. Work on them daily like any other skill.
Every want you chase brings some worry. Only chase the few that are worth it.
Where you live, who you are with and your work matter most. Choose them with care.
Read what you enjoy. If a book bores you, drop it and pick another.
Build a habit of reading for fun. You can carry almost any book on your phone.
Do the task instead of watching videos about it. Reading beats listening when time is short.
Choose who you work with before you choose the work. The right people make it work.
If you would not work with someone for years, do not start with them today.
Do not copy rivals. Serve people your own way, since no one can copy that.
Skip business fads. Learn how people think, how money works, and basic math instead.
Learn to sell and learn to make things. Doing both makes you very hard to beat.
Use your rare skills, own the result, and use tools that multiply your effort.
Turn what you do best into a service people can buy again and again.
Be really good at something and be yourself. People pay for that over time.
Build something that can grow without you. Over time, your good calls build your name.
Stop checking the numbers all day. Keep doing good work and the results will follow.
Your relationships shape your happiness most. Choose the people around you with care.
Set a value on your hour. Hand off or skip tasks worth less than that.
When you know you should do one thing but you are doing another, stop and switch.
Ignore hype and trends. Keep building the steady thing that gets better each year.
Most fights are about who looks important. Skip them and get back to real work.
No one else can make you healthy, rich or calm. Take charge of it yourself.
Skip any plan that promises fast money. Someone else is usually the one getting rich.
